name: High-pressure flow iron
function: Temporary high-pressure pipe, swivel joints, tees, crosses, check valves, plug valves, and relief valves with hammer unions that connect the missile, zipper manifold, and tree.

tabs.overview: Pup joints in 2 in., 3 in., and 4 in. nominal sizes with wing-nut hammer unions; swivel joints give the run flexibility; tees and crosses split flow; a pressure relief valve on the missile side protects the pumps and iron; check valves stop backflow to the pumps. Iron is tracked by serial number and inspected for wall loss.
tabs.engineering: Rated 10,000 or 15,000 psi cold working pressure; union figure numbers are vendor nomenclature and must not be mixed across pressure classes. Wall-thickness inspection and pressure testing are part of every job.
tabs.connections: Hammer unions throughout; flanged big-bore alternatives replace multiple lines.
tabs.safety: Line of fire during pumping; whip checks and restraints on every joint; never strike a pressurized union; erosion at elbows and swivels is the common failure.
tabs.operations: Laid out, made up with hammers, restrained, pressure tested to the job pressure before the first stage.
tabs.failure_modes: Wall loss from erosion, union seal leaks, mismatched union halves.

hazards.control: Pressure test before pumping; bleed down and verify zero before breaking any connection.
Restraints and whip checks on iron; exclusion zone around pressurized lines.
Tree saver in the wellhead; valves fully open or fully closed only; iron inspection.
Hands clear of wing nuts, handwheels, and actuator linkages during operation.
